column1: Adversarial review: Larkspur Ferries funding pack (draft 3)

column4: “You forecast 410,000 passengers in year two, yet the only evidence is one summer survey of 300 people at a single pier. Why should anyone believe the winter numbers?”
column5: Q12 cites the 2023 pier survey and a regional tourism growth figure of 4%.
column6: No winter data, no sensitivity range and no comparison with a similar route elsewhere.
column7: Add a low, central and high case, state the winter assumption plainly and cite one comparable route with its actual figures.

column4: “Q56 says two vessels cost 9.2m in total, Q16 budgets 8.1m and Q49 mentions a third hull. Which is it, and does the board know the figures disagree?”
column5: Q56 gives the supplier quote; Q16 was written before the quote arrived.
column6: Three answers give three different totals, which reads as a pack nobody checked end to end.
column7: Pick the supplier quote as the single source, correct Q16 and Q49 to match it, and add one table reconciling all fleet costs.

column4: “You say certification is in hand, but name no certifying body, no date and no fallback if the inspection fails. In hand could mean anything.”
column5: Q7 states that the operator holds a current licence for its existing route.
column6: The new vessels need their own certification and the pack is silent on timing.
column7: Name the certifying body, give the booked inspection window and say what happens to the launch date if it slips.

column4: “A 6.50 single fare is called affordable for commuters, with no reference to local wages or to what the bus costs for the same journey.”
column5: Q23 compares the fare with the tourist cruise price of 14.00.
column6: The comparison is with a leisure product, not with the commuter alternative.
column7: Compare the fare with the bus and rail price for the same journey and with median local hourly pay.

column4: “Forty-two crew are needed by launch and you currently employ nine. Where do thirty-three qualified crew come from in a region with a known shortage?”
column5: Q31 describes a training partnership with the harbour college.
column6: The college course takes eighteen months and launch is in eleven.
column7: Show the recruitment pipeline by month, including agency cover for the gap, and its cost.

column4: “The carbon saving assumes every passenger would otherwise drive alone. That is the most flattering assumption available and you have not defended it.”
column5: Q40 uses the national average car emissions figure.
column6: No evidence on what passengers actually do today; the saving could be half the stated figure.
column7: Use the survey's own travel-mode split, and present the saving as a range with the method in an annex.

column4: “Is the 2.4m match funding committed or merely hoped for? The wording moves between secured, expected and in discussion across three pages.”
column5: Q18 lists the funders and amounts in a table.
column6: Only one of the three funders has signed; the table does not say so.
column7: Add a status column to the funders table with the date of each signed letter, and use one word consistently.

column4: “The project board meets quarterly. On a build this size that means a problem can run for three months before anyone senior hears of it.”
column5: Q9 names the board members and their experience.
column6: No description of what is reported between meetings or who can stop spending.
column7: Describe the monthly report, the escalation route and the spending limit above which the board must approve.

column4: “Your whole timetable depends on a terminal you do not own, on a lease that ends two years before the loan does.”
column5: Q62 notes a good relationship with the port authority.
column6: A good relationship is not an option to renew; the lease end date is absent from the risk register.
column7: Seek a written option to renew, add the lease to the risk register and state the fallback pier.

column4: “The summary promises jobs for local people but the pack never defines local or commits to a number.”
column5: Q3 estimates 60 jobs in total across the operation.
column6: No definition, no target and no way to check afterwards.
column7: Define local by postcode area, commit to a share of roles and say how it will be reported each year.
